description:
The /fly HUD speed readout displays 'NaN km/s' for outer-planet missions (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, and any destination whose orbital radius exceeds ~1.5 AU) because the vis-viva semi-major axis is hardcoded to the Earth→Mars Hohmann transfer value. Inner-planet destinations (Mercury, Venus) produce finite but incorrect speeds for the same reason.

Expected: The HUD speed readout shows a finite, physically plausible heliocentric speed (km/s) consistent with a Hohmann transfer from Earth to the specific destination, for every destination in the /fly catalog. Earth→Mars missions are unchanged.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricKms MUST be derived using the per-destination Hohmann transfer semi-major axis (R_EARTH_AU + DEST_ORBITAL_AU) / 2, where DEST_ORBITAL_AU is the destination's orbital semi-major axis from the DESTINATIONS table (src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts). The fix MUST NOT add special cases per destination or clamping guards — the same expression must work for all non-Moon destinations by substituting DEST_ORBITAL_AU. [code-invariant: heliocentricSpeed(rAu, aTransferAu) in src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts requires aTransferAu = Hohmann transfer semi-major axis. For Earth→D Hohmann, aTransfer = (R_EARTH + a_D) / 2. a_D is DESTINATIONS[D].a for every destination.]
- For every Earth→Mars mission, heliocentricKms after the fix must be identical to the pre-fix value within numerical precision (no regression). [code-invariant: Mars missions currently produce the correct speed; the fix must not regress them. DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a for Mars = R_MARS_AU, so (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS['mars'].a) / 2 = (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU) / 2 — the formula generalizes.]
- For every mission in static/data/missions/{mars,jupiter,saturn,uranus,neptune,pluto,ceres} that loads into the /fly scene, data-helio-kms on the arc container element must be a finite number (not NaN, not Infinity) at every simDay. [reporter: Issue states: 'the HUD speed readout just says NaN km/s the whole way' for outer-planet missions.]
